posts.headline: Prices rose faster than expected in October
posts.source: Source: BLS Consumer Price Index, October 2026 (Nov 10 2026)
posts.caption:
Groceries, power bills and beef all cost more in October.

Consumer prices rose 0.4% in one month, more than economists expected, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Nov 10. Groceries rose 0.4%. Electricity rose 0.9%. Beef rose 0.9%.

One odd detail: BLS published no official 12-month rate this time, because last year's government shutdown stopped it collecting October 2025 data.

My take: one month is not a trend, but a 0.9% jump in a monthly bill is something a household budget feels.

Which bill has gone up most for you this year?

Source: BLS CPI, October 2026 (released Nov 10 2026); CNBC

#Inflation #Groceries #CostOfLiving

data.footnote: October 2026 vs September, seasonally adjusted. Released Nov 10 2026. No official 12-month rate.

posts.headline: Myth: checking your own credit score lowers it
posts.caption:
Looking at your own credit score does not cost you a single point.

When you check your own score or report, it counts as a soft inquiry. Soft inquiries do not affect your score.

A hard inquiry happens when a lender pulls your credit because you applied for a loan or a card. That can lower a score a little for a while.

You can get free credit reports from each of the three bureaus at AnnualCreditReport.com.

My take: the people who check most often tend to catch errors earliest.

When did you last look at your credit report?

Source: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau

#CreditScore #Credit #MoneyMyths

data.dek: Checking your own score is a soft inquiry, and soft inquiries do not count. Only a lender's pull for an application is a hard inquiry.

posts.headline: Oil jumped 3% after attacks on Saudi energy sites
posts.source: Source: Reuters, oil settlement prices, Nov 12 2026
posts.caption:
Oil prices rose sharply on Thursday after attacks on energy sites in Saudi Arabia.

Houthi forces claimed strikes on a pipeline pumping station, an oil facility in Yanbu and an Aramco building in Riyadh, Reuters reported. Brent crude settled up 3.3% at $95.82 a barrel. US crude rose 2.6% to $88.74.

Crude is the biggest single cost in a gallon of gasoline, so moves like this can reach the pump if they last.

My take: one day's jump is not a price at the pump yet. It is worth watching, not panicking over.

Have you noticed gas prices moving where you live?

Source: Reuters, Nov 12 2026

#Oil #GasPrices #Energy

posts.headline: Same $10,000. Very different interest
posts.source: Source: Follow the Money calculation, simple interest, one year
posts.caption:
Where you park your emergency fund can be worth hundreds of dollars a year.

At 0.01% APY, $10,000 earns about $1 in a year. At 1% it earns $100. At 4% it earns $400.

These are example rates, not quotes. Savings rates vary by bank and change over time, so check what yours pays today.

My take: an emergency fund should be safe and easy to reach. It does not have to earn almost nothing.

Do you know the rate on your savings account?

Source: Follow the Money calculation, example rates, one year, before tax

#Savings #EmergencyFund #PersonalFinance

posts.headline: How a Fed rate hike would reach your card bill
posts.caption:
Fed officials are openly discussing raising rates at their December meeting.

After October's hotter than expected inflation report, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a half-point hike should be considered at the Dec 8-9 meeting, CNBC reported. Nothing has been decided.

If the Fed does raise rates, most credit cards follow. Card rates are usually tied to the prime rate, which moves with the Fed.

My take: a card balance is the debt most exposed to a hike.

Do you know whether your card rate is fixed or variable?

Source: CNBC, Nov 10 2026; Federal Reserve

#InterestRates #CreditCards #FederalReserve

steps.label: The Fed raises its target rate
steps.detail: Its next meeting is Dec 8-9. Officials have said a hike is on the table.

steps.label: Banks raise the prime rate
steps.detail: Prime usually moves by the same amount within days.

steps.label: Your card APR follows prime
steps.detail: Variable card rates are prime plus a margin, so they rise too.

steps.label: Savings rates may rise too
steps.detail: Banks can pay more on savings, but they do not have to.

posts.headline: Mortgage rates fell for a fourth straight week
posts.source: Source: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey, Nov 12 2026
posts.caption:
Mortgage rates eased again, but they are still well above a year ago.

The average 30-year fixed rate was 7.11% this week, down from 7.18% the week before, Freddie Mac said Nov 12. It was the fourth straight weekly drop. A year ago the average was 6.24%.

The 15-year fixed averaged 6.45%.

My take: small weekly drops add up for buyers, but the gap from last year is what most budgets still feel.

Is a rate change shaping your housing plans?

Source: Freddie Mac PMMS, week of Nov 12 2026

#Mortgage #Housing #InterestRates

data.footnote: Weekly averages, Freddie Mac survey released Nov 12 2026.

posts.headline: Pay $100 a month, or $50 a month?
posts.source: Source: Follow the Money calculation, 21% APR, no new charges
posts.caption:
Doubling a card payment can cut the interest by about two thirds.

On a $2,000 balance at 21% APR with no new charges, paying $50 a month takes 70 months and about $1,470 in interest. Paying $100 a month takes 25 months and about $483.

That is close to $1,000 kept, and the debt is gone almost four years sooner.

My take: an extra $50 a month on a card is one of the surest returns there is.

Have you ever worked out what a card balance really costs you?

Source: Follow the Money calculation, 21% APR, interest monthly

posts.kicker: What your score is made of
posts.headline: Paying on time matters most to your score
posts.source: Source: myFICO, what's in your FICO score
posts.caption:
More than a third of a FICO score comes down to one habit: paying on time.

FICO says payment history makes up 35% of a typical score. Amounts owed is 30%. Length of credit history is 15%. New credit and credit mix are 10% each.

That is why a single late payment can hurt more than opening a new card.

My take: autopay for at least the minimum is the cheapest insurance your score can get.

Which part of your score surprised you most?

Source: myFICO

#CreditScore #FICO #Credit

data.unit: Share of a typical FICO score

posts.headline: What $200 a month can grow to
posts.source: Source: Follow the Money calculation, 6% a year, monthly
posts.caption:
Time does most of the work when you invest a steady amount.

Put away $200 a month and assume 6% a year. After 10 years you have put in $24,000 and it has grown to about $32,800. After 30 years, $72,000 in grows to about $200,900. After 40 years, $96,000 in grows to about $398,300.

Real returns go up and down. 6% is an example, not a promise.

My take: the earliest dollars do the heaviest lifting.

When did you start saving for the long term?

Source: Follow the Money calculation, 6% a year, compounded monthly
Educational only — not financial advice.

posts.headline: Myth: a debit card protects you like a credit card
posts.caption:
If your card is stolen, the law treats debit and credit very differently.

With a credit card, your liability for unauthorized charges is capped at $50, the FTC says. With a debit card, it depends on how fast you report: up to $50 within two business days, up to $500 after that, and possibly everything after 60 days from your statement.

And with debit, it is your own cash that is missing while it gets sorted out.

My take: speed of reporting is the whole game with a debit card.

Do you use debit or credit for online shopping?

Source: Federal Trade Commission

#DebitCard #Fraud #Banking

data.dek: Credit card fraud liability is capped at $50. Debit card liability can reach $500 or more if you report it late.
